s1.syndrome_frame: Painless testicular swelling with associated epididymal involvement and adrenal gland abnormalities
salient_findings: Enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
key_facts: 82-year-old man
Painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration
No systemic symptoms
History of glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty
Medications: dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride
Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
Ipsilateral hydrocele
Swelling persisted after 10 days of amoxicillin–clavulanate
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed testicular pathology
New bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement
Adrenal nodules were absent on a CT scan 3 years earlier
18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake in the right testis
No uptake in the adrenal glands
Normal laboratory evaluation
Negative serologies for active HCV and EBV
Positive for past EBV

shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and testicular ultrasound findings

shortlist.why_kept: New bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement and testicular pathology

shortlist.why_kept: Testicular swelling and epididymal involvement with associated adrenal gland abnormalities

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of painless testicular swelling and the ultrasound findings of testicular enlargement and inhomogeneity, along with the intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT, are consistent with a testicular tumor. The absence of systemic symptoms and the normal laboratory evaluation make a metastatic process less likely. Leydig cell tumors are known to cause testicular enlargement and can present with hormonal effects, but in this case, the patient's normal laboratory evaluation and lack of systemic symptoms suggest a localized process.

rejected.label: Testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory findings, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with testicular swelling and may have elevated LDH or β2-microglobulin, but the intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT and the patient's age make Leydig cell tumor more likely

rejected.label: Adrenal metastasis from testicular cancer
rejected.why: The adrenal nodules are new and bilateral, but the lack of uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT and the normal laboratory evaluation make this less likely

rejected.label: Testicular sex cord-stromal tumor
rejected.why: This is a broad category that includes Leydig cell tumors, but Leydig cell tumor is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's presentation

rejected.label: Testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory findings, which are not present in this case
